challenge.title: A morning of errands
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you withdraw cash at the bank, ask the cost of sending a parcel, and top up your phone balance, and ask for directions between the stops.
required_elements: a request at the bank such as أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْحَبَ مَبْلَغًا نَقْدِيًّا
a question about the post office with أَيْنَ
a question about a price with كَمْ تَكْلِفَةُ
a request to top up the phone balance with شَحْنَ رَصِيدِي
a polite word such as مِنْ فَضْلِك or شُكْرًا

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْحَبَ مَبْلَغًا نَقْدِيًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. ureedu an asHaba mablaghan naqdiyyan.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I want to withdraw some cash.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. How much?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مِئَةُ دِينَار. وَأَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الْبَرِيد مِنْ فَضْلِك؟
dialogue.transliteration: mi2atu deenaar. wa ayna maktabu al-bareed min faDlik?
dialogue.english: A hundred dinars. And where is the post office, please?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فِي آخِرِ الشَّارِع، بِجَانِبِ مَحَلِّ الْهَوَاتِف.
dialogue.transliteration: fee aakhiri ash-shaari3, bijaanibi maHalli al-hawaatif.
dialogue.english: At the end of the street, next to the phone shop.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ طَرْدًا. كَمْ تَكْلِفَةُ الشَّحْن؟
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu an ursila Tardan. kam taklifatu ash-shaHn?
dialogue.english: I want to send a parcel. How much is the shipping?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Twenty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: I also want to top up my balance.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Please. How much do you want to add?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Thank you. May Allah reward you with good.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And you too.

reply.english: I will issue you a new card.

phrases.arabic: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُحَوِّلَ مَبْلَغًا إِلَى هَذَا الْحِسَاب
phrases.transliteration: ureedu an uHawwila mablaghan ilaa haadha al-Hisaab

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أُرِيدُ فَتْحَ حِسَابٍ مَصْرِفِيّ.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I want to open a bank account.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. تَفَضَّلْ، اِمْلَأْ هَذَا النَّمُوذَج. هَلْ مَعَكَ بِطَاقَةُ الْهُوِيَّة؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. tafaDDal, imla2 haadha an-namoodhaj. hal ma3aka biTaaqatu al-huwiyya?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Please, fill in this form. Do you have your ID card?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Yes, here it is. Where do I sign?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: هُنَا، عَلَى الْخَطّ. مَاذَا تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَفْعَلَ أَيْضًا؟
dialogue.transliteration: hunaa, 3alaa al-khaTT. maadhaa tureedu an taf3ala aydan?
dialogue.english: Here, on the line. What else do you want to do?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أُحَوِّلَ مَبْلَغًا إِلَى هَذَا الْحِسَاب.
dialogue.transliteration: wa ureedu an uHawwila mablaghan ilaa haadha al-Hisaab.
dialogue.english: And I want to transfer money to this account.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Here you are. How much is the transfer fee?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Fine. And where is the ATM?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Next to the door. Here is your receipt.

pair.english: Do you have your ID card?
I want to withdraw some cash.
How much is the transfer fee?

lessons.culture: Banks in most Arab countries open in the morning and often close by mid-afternoon, and many are closed on Friday. You need your ID card or passport to open an account, and the clerk will ask you to sign the form. Cash is still common for daily shopping, so ATMs are everywhere and exchange offices often sit near the banks.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: 'Where's the ATM?'
exercises.tip: ayna opens the question, then the machine.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'كَمْ رُسُومُ _____؟' (How much is the transfer fee?)

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'هَلْ مَعَكَ بِطَاقَةُ الْهُوِيَّة؟'. Say: yes, here it is.
exercises.tip: hadhihi hiya means here it is, said of a feminine thing.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كَمْ رُسُومُ التَّحْوِيل؟'. Say: five dinars.
exercises.tip: khamsa is five; danaaneer is dinars.

reply.english: At the end of the street.

phrases.arabic: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ طَرْدًا إِلَى بَلَدِي
phrases.transliteration: ureedu an ursila Tardan ilaa baladee

reply.english: Yes, this is the tracking number.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ طَرْدًا إِلَى بَلَدِي.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. ureedu an ursila Tardan ilaa baladee.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I want to send a parcel to my country.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Put it on the scale.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Three kilograms, and the shipping is twenty dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: About two weeks. Write the address here.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ. وَأُرِيدُ طَابِعًا بَرِيدِيًّا مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: tafaDDal. wa ureedu Taabi3an bareediyyan min faDlik.
dialogue.english: Here you are. And I want a stamp, please.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Here you are. Do you want anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Thank you. Where is the mailbox?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: In front of the office. Goodbye.

pair.english: How long does it take to arrive?

response.english: At the end of the street.
Yes, this is the tracking number.

lessons.culture: Many Arab post offices also take bill payments and sell stamps, and the clerk weighs a parcel at the counter to set the price. Street addresses are not always numbered, so people often use a PO box or add a nearby landmark. Private courier companies are popular for fast international parcels.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كَمْ يَسْتَغْرِقُ الْوُصُول؟'. Say: about two weeks.

reply.english: Please, do you have your passport?
How many gigabytes do you want?
How much do you want to add?
This is your number, save it.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أُرِيدُ شِرَاءَ شَرِيحَةِ اتِّصَال.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I want to buy a SIM card.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. تَفَضَّلْ، هَلْ مَعَكَ جَوَازُ السَّفَر؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. tafaDDal, hal ma3aka jawaazu as-safar?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Please, do you have your passport?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، هَذَا هُوَ. وَأُرِيدُ أَيْضًا بَاقَةَ إِنْتَرْنِت.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, haadha huwa. wa ureedu aydan baaqata internet.
dialogue.english: Yes, here it is. I also want an internet package.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: عَشَرَةَ جِيجَابَايْت. كَمْ سِعْرُ هَذِهِ الْبَاقَة؟
dialogue.english: Ten gigabytes. How much is this package?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And how long is it valid?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: شَاشَةُ هَاتِفِي مَكْسُورَة. كَمْ تَكْلِفَةُ الْإِصْلَاح؟
dialogue.transliteration: shaashatu haatifee maksoora. kam taklifatu al-iSlaaH?
dialogue.english: My phone screen is broken. How much is the repair?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Fifty dinars. We can repair it tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا. هَلْ يُمْكِنُ تَشْغِيلُ الْخَدَمَةِ الْيَوْم؟
dialogue.transliteration: Hasanan. hal yumkinu tashgheelu al-khidmati al-yawm?
dialogue.english: Fine. Can the service be activated today?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Yes, within an hour. Thank you.

pair.english: Does this phone take two SIM cards?

lessons.culture: In many Arab countries you buy a SIM card at a phone shop or a kiosk, and the seller asks for your passport or ID card to register the line. Most people use prepaid balance that they top up with a recharge card or an app, and internet packages are sold by the month. Phone shops also repair screens and sell chargers and cases.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أُرِيدُ شَحْنَ _____' (I want to top up my balance.)
exercises.tip: raSeed is a balance; -ee means my.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'كَمْ سِعْرُ هَذِهِ الْبَاقَة؟'. Say: ten dinars a month.
exercises.tip: fee ash-shahr means per month.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'هَلْ يُمْكِنُ تَشْغِيلُ الْخَدَمَةِ الْيَوْم؟'. Say: yes, within an hour.
exercises.tip: khilaala means within; saa3a is an hour.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Hello, I need an ambulance!

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: What happened? Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: I don't speak Arabic well.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: لَا بَأْس، تَكَلَّمْ بِبُطْء. أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa ba2s, takallam bibuT2. ayna anta?
dialogue.english: It's fine, speak slowly. Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا هُوَ الْعُنْوَان. أَسْرِعْ مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: haadha huwa al-3unwaan. asri3 min faDlik.
dialogue.english: This is the address. Please hurry.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: نَحْنُ فِي الطَّرِيق. اِبْقَ عَلَى الْخَطّ.
dialogue.english: We are on the way. Stay on the line.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Okay. There is also a fire.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Get out of the building at once.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: سَأَخْرُجُ الْآن. مَا رَقْمُ الطَّوَارِئ لِلشُّرْطَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: sa-akhruju al-aan. maa raqmu aT-Tawaari2 lish-shurTa?
dialogue.english: I will go out now. What is the emergency number for the police?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: We will send the police too. Do not worry.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And where is the nearest hospital?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: عَلَى بُعْدِ خَمْسِ دَقَائِق. الطَّبِيبُ قَادِم.
dialogue.english: Five minutes away. The doctor is coming.

lessons.culture: Emergency numbers differ from country to country, so learn the local ones when you arrive: for example 911 in Jordan, 997 for an ambulance in Saudi Arabia, and 122 for the police in Egypt. Say your location first and speak slowly and clearly, since the operator needs the address before anything else. Staying calm and keeping the line open lets help reach you faster.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى _____' (I need a doctor.)

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'مَا رَقْمُ _____؟' (What is the emergency number?)

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'اِتَّصِلْ بِالشُّرْطَة'. Say: where are you?.
exercises.tip: ayna anta asks where you are.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'أَسْرِعْ مِنْ فَضْلِك'. Say: we are on the way.
exercises.tip: naHnu fee aT-Tareeq means we are on the way.

reply.english: We will take you to the hospital.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَقَعَ حَادِث! اِصْطَدَمَتْ سَيَّارَتِي بِسَيَّارَةٍ أُخْرَى.
dialogue.transliteration: waqa3a Haadith! iSTadamat sayyaaratee bisayyaaratin ukhraa.
dialogue.english: There has been an accident! My car hit another car.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Yes, one person. My leg hurts.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Do not move. I will call the ambulance.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا. أَحْضِرْ حَقِيبَةَ الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّة مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: Hasanan. aHDir Haqeebata al-is3aafaati al-awwaliyya min faDlik.
dialogue.english: Okay. Bring the first aid kit, please.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: Here it is. Here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى ضِمَادَة. وَاتَّصِلْ بِأَهْلِي مِنْ فَضْلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: aHtaaju ilaa Dimaada. wattaSil bi-ahlee min faDlik.
dialogue.english: I need a bandage. And please call my family.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا هُوَ الرَّقْم. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ أَنَا بِخَيْر.
dialogue.transliteration: haadha huwa ar-raqm. al-Hamdu lillaah anaa bikhayr.
dialogue.english: This is the number. Thank Allah, I am fine.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى سَلَامَتِك. وَصَلَتِ الشُّرْطَة.
dialogue.english: Thank Allah for your safety. The police have arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أُرِيدُ تَقْرِيرًا مِنَ الشُّرْطَة. هَذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ التَّأْمِين.
dialogue.transliteration: ureedu taqreeran mina ash-shurTa. hadhihi biTaaqatu at-ta2meen.
dialogue.english: I want a report from the police. This is my insurance card.

response.english: We will take you to the hospital.

pair.english: I want a report from the police.

lessons.culture: After a road accident, do not move the car until the police say so, unless it blocks traffic. In many Arab countries the police must write a report before an insurance company will pay, so ask for it at the scene. Emergency numbers differ by country, for example 997 for an ambulance in Saudi Arabia and 123 in Egypt, so check the local one. Stay calm and help anyone hurt without moving them.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'أَنَا بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه'. Say: thank Allah for your safety.
exercises.tip: salaama is safety; 3alaa salaamatik wishes you well after trouble.

exercises.prompt: You hear: 'أَحْضِرْ حَقِيبَةَ الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّة'. Say: here it is.
exercises.tip: haa hiya means here it is.

phrases.arabic: أَعْلِنْ ذَلِكَ بِمُكَبِّرِ الصَّوْتِ مِنْ فَضْلِك
phrases.transliteration: a3lin dhaalika bimukabbiri aS-Sawti min faDlik

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. My child is lost!

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. How old is he?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: عُمْرُهُ خَمْسُ سَنَوَات. يَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا أَحْمَر.
dialogue.english: He is five years old. He is wearing a red shirt.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: عِنْدَ مَدْخَلِ السُّوق. سَاعِدْنِي فِي الْبَحْثِ عَنْه.
dialogue.english: At the market entrance. Please help me find him.

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: We will search together. Do you have a photo?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، هَذِهِ صُورَتُه. أَيْنَ مَكْتَبُ الِاسْتِعْلَامَات؟
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, hadhihi Sooratuhu. ayna maktabu al-isti3laamaat?
dialogue.english: Yes, this is his photo. Where is the information desk?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.english: On the ground floor. We will announce it now.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: أَعْلِنْ ذَلِكَ بِمُكَبِّرِ الصَّوْتِ مِنْ فَضْلِك. هَلْ يُوجَدُ حَارِسُ أَمْنٍ هُنَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: a3lin dhaalika bimukabbiri aS-Sawti min faDlik. hal yoojadu Haarisu amnin hunaa?
dialogue.english: Please announce it on the loudspeaker. Is there a security guard here?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، عِنْدَ الْبَوَّابَة. اُنْظُرْ هُنَاكَ، وَجَدْنَاهُ!
dialogue.english: Yes, at the gate. Look over there, we found him!

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Thank Allah! Thank you for your help.

pair.english: Where did you see him last?

lessons.culture: In a crowded place, go straight to the information desk or a security guard, who can announce the child's name on the loudspeaker. Teach children early to say their parent's name and phone number, and keep a recent photo on your phone. Emergency numbers differ by country, so learn the local one when you arrive. Stay calm so you can describe the clothes and the last place you saw the child.

exercises.tip: maktab is a desk; isti3laamaat is information.

exercises.prompt: Which one means 'Where did you see him last?'
exercises.tip: ra2aytahu is you saw him; aakhira marra is last time.

exercises.tip: saa3idnee is help me; 3anhu is for him.

exercises.tip: kam 3umruhu asks his age.
